title: Summer Games
build: The PAL G64 of Epyx's disk (directory "SUMMER GAMES"): the boot file SUMMER GAMES and SGLOAD, the engine B unpacked to $0C00-$3EFF, the opening ceremony A, six event files D, E, F, H, I and K each unpacked over $4000 upward (swimming over $1000-$BEFF), the world records WR and DEFAULT, and the unused files L and M; a second PAL image and an NTSC image were supplied too

records.c: The skeet field as a multicolour bitmap, 8000 bytes ($4000-$5F3F) in VIC bank 1: sky, clouds, hills, the two trap houses and the yellow semicircle of the eight shooting stations. $73AF points the VIC at it ($DD00 bank 1, $D018 = $80)
Bitmap character rows 3-5: sky and clouds
Bitmap character rows 6-8: the last of the sky and the blue hills on the horizon
Bitmap character rows 9-11: the line of trees and the tops of the two trap houses at the left and right edges
Bitmap character rows 12-14: the trap houses' lower halves and the grass inside the arc, with the station posts
Bitmap character rows 15-17: grass and the sides of the arc with stations
Bitmap character rows 18-20: the bottom of the arc and the middle station
Bitmap character rows 21-23: a strip of grass, then the black band where draw_char ($7B05) writes the name and score text at run time
Bitmap character row 24: the prompt row, drawn by draw_char at run time
The 192 bytes between the end of the bitmap and the screen at $6000: nothing in the module reads them

Screen RAM of the bitmap ($6000-$63E7): in multicolour bitmap mode each byte gives two of the colours of its 8 x 8 cell, so these 1000 bytes are part of the picture. Rows 0-12: sky, hills, trees and the tops of the houses
Screen colours, rows 13-24: grass and stations, then the three text rows, whose cells draw_char ($7B05) recolours at run time

Screen RAM from row 22, column 0: the colour cells of the three text rows under the field. draw_char ($7B05) writes the text colour from $7AA9 here for each cell it draws, indexed by cell number 0-119
Colour cells of text row 24, the prompt row. next_player ($7030) clears its 40 cells to black on black, which hides the "PUSH BUTTON" prompt

The eight sprite pointers at the end of the screen ($6000 + $3F8). setup_screen ($73AF) sets them to $A0-$A7, so sprite n's shape is at $4000 + 64 x ($A0 + n): $6800 upward. Sprites 4 and 5 both point at $A4, the shadow
Sprite 1's pointer, set to $A1: the right house's clay at $6840
Sprite 2's pointer, set to $A2: the left house's clay at $6880
Sprite 3's pointer, set to $A3 ($68C0); sprite 3 is never turned on
Sprite 4's pointer, set to $A4: the shadow at $6900, under the right clay
Sprite 5's pointer, also set to $A4: the same shadow shape, under the left clay
Sprite 6's pointer, set to $A6 ($6980); sprite 6 is never turned on
Sprite 7's pointer, set to $A7: the shot disc at $69C0
The bitmap's colour RAM picture, 1000 bytes. copy_colours ($7B4B) copies it to $D800 when the event starts
The field's background colour (5, green). The raster interrupt ($707A) restores $D021 from here after the black band of the text rows

Bytes the module file carries after the colour picture and around the sprite buffers, $67E9-$67FF and $6A00-$6FFF: the same 256-byte pattern over and over, the look of uninitialised RAM. Nothing reads them; the sprite buffers at $6800 are written over at run time
Sprite 0's shape (pointer $A0): the gun sight, a ring with a dot, copied from $7517 by setup_screen
Sprite 1's shape (pointer $A1): the clay from the right-hand house. A fresh whole clay is copied from $75BA when a target is pulled ($70D5), and break_clays ($74C8) copies the shatter frames over it
Sprite 2's shape (pointer $A2): the clay from the left-hand house, filled the same way as $6840
The shape sprites 4 and 5 share (pointer $A4): the clays' shadows on the grass, copied from $7597 by setup_screen
Sprite 7's shape (pointer $A7): a filled disc, the spread of the shot, copied from $7557. It is shown for one frame where the sight is when the button is pressed, and a clay it overlaps counts as hit
Leftover bytes, the same repeating pattern as $67E9: nothing reads them
Leftover bytes to the end of the bitmap bank, the same repeating pattern as $67E9: nothing reads them

Module entry, reached from the engine's loader at $0900. Copies the colour picture, takes the number of players from $081E, zeroes the score, installs the raster interrupt, draws the screen, turns on multicolour bitmap mode, sets up the first shot and the first "PUSH BUTTON TO BEGIN" prompt, then idles at $702D: everything after this runs in the interrupt at $707A
The main program's idle loop: the whole event runs in the raster interrupt

Starts the next shooter's round (called when the button is pressed at a "PUSH BUTTON TO BEGIN" prompt). Zeroes targets and hits and the station and shot counters, counts $7A9F down, and when no shooter is left jumps back to the engine at $0900. Otherwise it takes the shooter from the shuffled order at $7AA1, finds the record at $0800 + 32 x shooter, prints the 16-character name at the start of row 22 in light red, and blanks the prompt row

The raster interrupt, at line $E1 every frame (installed by $7386 through the KERNAL vector $0314). Turns the background black and multicolour off for the band of text rows from line $E3 to $FA, then back on in green; counts frames at $7A99; prints the score and plays both sound voices. Then, by the state at $7A94: 1 or 0, wait for the button (1: begin the next shooter's round; 0: pull the target); $FF, a clay is in the air: move it and its shadow, move the sight, fire, test for hits. Ends through the KERNAL's register pull and RTI
The button was pressed while waiting. State 1 becomes 0: start the next shooter (next_player, next_shot). State 0 becomes $FF: pull, at $70D5
Pull: copies a whole clay over both clay sprites and adds the targets thrown to $7A9C in decimal, 1 for a single and 2 for a double (shot type 6)

Flight, one frame: steps both clays along their paths. The left house's clay is sprite 2 with its shadow, sprite 5: x from $76CE and y from $7749 and $77C4. The right house's is sprite 1 with shadow 4: x from $783F, y from $78BA and $7935. When $783F's path reaches its $FF end the shot is over and next_shot ($71D9) sets up the next. Both paths are stepped even when only one clay is shown
Every frame of a shot: move the sight by the joystick, then either finish a shot's flash (look for hits) or look for a new shot

The flash is over: hide the shot disc (sprite 7) and read the sprite-to-sprite collision register. For each of sprites 1 and 2 the disc touched that is not already breaking: hide its shadow, start a five-step break at $7A9A, and add 1 to the hits at $7A9D in decimal

A new press of the button fires, if a shell is left at $7A61: the last shell plays the voice-1 bang ($7BA8), the first of a double the voice-2 bang ($7C19). Shows the shot disc, sprite 7, for one frame
Reads $D01E once to clear the collision latch, then leaves the interrupt by pulling Y, X and A and returning
AND masks for $D015. Indexed 0-1 from $71D5 by a hit they hide sprites 4 and 5, the shadows; indexed from $71D7 by break_clays they hide sprites 1 and 2, the clays
The second pair of $71D5's masks ($FD, $FB): clear sprite 1 or sprite 2

Sets up the next shot from the station list at $7A64. A zero there ends a station: the next station begins, and after the eighth the round ends (end_round, $725B). Gives one shell, two for a double (type 6). Puts the sight at the station's starting place ($7A7F, $7A87), shows the clay sprites and shadows the shot type names (bits 1 and 2, and 4 and 5), and clears the collision latch, timers, flight steps and the sight's droop

The shooter's 25 targets are done. Starts the short tune on voice 2 (the longer one after the last shooter), sets the state to 1 and the text colour to yellow, and prints on row 24 either the next shooter's name and "PUSH BUTTON TO BEGIN" two cells after it, or after the last shooter "PUSH BUTTON TO EXIT SKEET SHOOTING". Also run once at the start, for the first prompt

Reads the button on the joystick at $DC00 with a four-frame lockout after each change. Returns Z set (A = 0) on a new press, A = $10 on a new release, and A = $FF with Z clear when nothing has changed or the lockout is running

Moves the sight one step a frame by the joystick at $DC00: x between 6 and $50, y between $10 and $43. When the stick is left alone, on every other frame a counter at $7A60 runs 0-3 and the sight droops one step lower each time it wraps, so a sight held still sinks slowly until y = $43
Puts sprites 0 (the sight) and 7 (the shot disc) at the sight's place: x = 4 x $7A95, with bit 8 of both in $D010; y = 3 x $7A96 + 1 + the droop counter
Waits for raster line $64, turns off the CIA's timer interrupt, enables the raster interrupt at line $E1, sets bitmap mode ($D011 = $3B) and points the KERNAL's IRQ vector at skeet_irq ($707A)

Turns on all eight sprites, chooses VIC bank 1 and the screen at $6000 with the bitmap at $4000, makes the I/O visible, draws the three text rows from $79E8, and shuffles the shooting order at $7AA1 with the CIA timer's low byte as the random number. Then copies the sight, the shot disc and the shadow into their sprites, sets the sprite pointers and colours (sight brown, clays red and blue, shadows grey, disc black) and the starting positions
The shooting order: fill $7AA1 with 0-7, then swap each of the first $7A9F entries with one chosen by the CIA timer at $DC04 (reduced below the number of players by repeated subtraction)

On every fourth frame, steps each breaking clay (timers at $7A9A) one frame on: copies the next of five shatter frames, chosen through $750D and $7512, into the clay's sprite; when the timer reaches 0 the clay is hidden
High bytes of the five break frames, read with $7512's low bytes: $75BA, $75FB, $7634, $7664, $768E. Frame 4 is shown first and frame 0 last
Low bytes of the five break frames (see $750D)
The gun sight's sprite: a ring 24 pixels wide with a small cross in the middle, 64 bytes, copied to $6800
The shot's sprite: a filled disc the size of the sight's ring, 64 bytes, copied to $69C0 for sprite 7
The shadow's sprite: a small flat oval low in the frame, copied to $6900 for sprites 4 and 5

The clay and its break: frame 0 at $75BA is the whole clay, copied over both clay sprites at each pull. The shatter frames at $75FB, $7634, $7664 and $768E overlap one another, each 64 bytes long but starting fewer than 64 bytes apart, since their ends are blank
The left house's clay, x position for each frame of flight (sprites 2 and 5), stepped from index 1: rising by 3 from $1C, wrapping past 255 (bit 8 is set in $D010 when it reads 0), then held at $5A
The left house's clay, y for sprite 2: the value x 2 + $6A. Falls from $0D to 3 and rises again to 9: the clay climbs and drops. The run of $44 at the end puts it below the screen
The left clay's shadow, y for sprite 5: the value x 2 + $6A. Moves slowly up the grass from $14 to $0D, then $47 puts it off the screen
The right house's clay, x position for each frame (sprites 1 and 4): falling by 3 from $5A, with bit 8 cleared in $D010 when it reads 0. The $FF at $78B9 ends the flight of both clays
The right house's clay, y for sprite 1: the value x 2 + $0D, from $3F down to $18 and on
The right clay's shadow, y for sprite 4: the value x 2 + $6D
Base address end_round indexes from $50 to print the exit prompt, so its text starts at $79B0; the bytes from $7960 to $79AF belong to the shadow table at $7935
The last 16 entries of the right clay's shadow table ($7935), all $44, below the screen
"PUSH BUTTON TO EXIT SKEET SHOOTING", ended by $FF: the prompt after the last shooter
"PUSH BUTTON TO BEGIN", ended by $FF, printed after the next shooter's name
The three text rows under the field, 120 characters drawn last to first: "SKEET SHOOTING" and "TARGETS:" on row 22, "HITS:" on row 23, row 24 blank
The sight's droop counter, 0-3: adds to the sight's y, and each wrap moves the sight one step lower (move_sight)
Shells left for this shot: 1, or 2 for a double
The station, 0-7
Index into the station list at $7A64

The shots, station by station, each station ended by 0. 4 is a clay from the left house, 2 from the right, 6 both at once (a double). Stations 1-8: 4 6 / 4 2 6 / 4 2 6 / 4 2 / 4 2 6 / 4 2 6 / 6 / 2 4, which with doubles counted twice is 25 targets
The sight's starting x at each of the eight stations
The sight's starting y at each of the eight stations
The button's last state, bit 4 of $DC00 (fire_edge)
fire_edge's lockout counter: 4 frames after each change of the button
The left clay's step along its flight tables
The right clay's step along its flight tables; the end of its table ends the shot
The shot in play: 2, 4 or 6, from $7A64
1 = waiting to begin a shooter's round, 0 = waiting for the pull, $FF = clays in the air
The sight's x, 6-$50 (x 4 on the screen)
The sight's y, $10-$43 (x 3 on the screen)
Scratch byte used by most routines
The cell of the last letter of the next shooter's name, for placing "PUSH BUTTON TO BEGIN" after it
Frame counter, counted by the interrupt
The break timers of the two clays (here sprite 1, at $7A9B sprite 2): 5 on a hit, down to 0
The break timer of the second clay (see $7A9A)
Targets thrown to this shooter, in binary-coded decimal
Targets hit, in binary-coded decimal; copied into the shooter's record at $0814
The shot disc's timer: 1 while the disc shows, for one frame
Shooters still to shoot; from $081E, the number of players, at the start
The offset of the shooter's record from $0800: 32 x the shooter's number
The shooting order, eight player numbers, shuffled at the start
The text colour draw_char writes into the screen: $A0 light red for names, $10 white for scores and labels, $70 yellow for prompts

Prints the targets thrown (row 22, columns 37-38) and hits (row 23, columns 37-38) in white, a leading 0 left blank, and stores the hits in the shooter's record: two digits as characters at $0814 and $0815 and the decimal value at $0816

Draws character A (its low six bits) into text cell X (0-119, three rows of 40 from row 22) of the bitmap: copies the glyph from the character ROM at $D000, seen by clearing bit 2 of $01, starting one byte early so the letter sits one pixel lower, and writes the colour from $7AA9
Copies the colour picture at $6400-$67E7 to colour RAM at $D800
Copies bytes from ($10) to ($12) until the source reaches ($14)
Sets voice 2's envelope and the volume, and starts voice 2 on a tune from $7C92: at offset 4, or at $20 after the last shooter, with the sawtooth waveform ($20)
Sets voice 1's envelope and starts voice 1 on the bang at the start of $7C92

Plays voice 1 each frame: holds each note for its length, releases the gate for 10 frames, then reads the next entry of $7C92 (frequency high, frequency low, length) with noise ($81). A negative entry ends the sound
Voice 1: frames left of the note
Voice 1: frames left of the release between notes
Voice 1: index into $7C92; negative when silent
Voice 2's waveform: $20 sawtooth for the tunes, $80 noise for the bang
Sets voice 2's envelope and the volume and starts voice 2 on the bang at the start of $7C92, with noise
Plays voice 2 each frame, as voice1_step does voice 1, with the waveform from $7C18
Voice 2: frames left of the note
Voice 2: frames left of the release
Voice 2: index into $7C92; negative when silent

The sound list, entries of frequency high, low and length in frames, each sound ended by $FF. At 0: the bang. At 4: the three-times-repeated phrase after a shooter's round. At $20: the closing phrase after the last shooter
30 bytes in groups of four and the end of the module's file: nothing reads them
